title: The lifeless body of Claude Jutra was finally found in the Saint Lawrence River near Cap-Santé.
text: The St. Lawrence River is a large international river in the middle latitudes of North America connecting the Great Lakes with the North Atlantic Ocean.

title: Provincial premiers agree to Meech Lake Accord.
text: The Meech Lake Accord was a series of proposed amendments to the Constitution of Canada negotiated in 1987 by Prime Minister Brian Mulroney and all 10 Canadian provincial premiers. It was intended to persuade the government of Quebec to symbolically endorse the 1982 constitutional amendments by providing for some decentralization of the Canadian federation.

title: Rick Hansen returns home to Vancouver after his Man in Motion world tour.
text: Richard Marvin Hansen is a Canadian Paralympic track-and-field athlete, activist, and philanthropist for people with disabilities. He represented Canada at 1980 and 1984 Summer Paralympics, and is a three-time Gold medalist.

title: a bill to restore the death penalty was defeated by the House of Commons in a 148–127 vote, in which Prime Minister Brian Mulroney, Minister of Justice Ray Hnatyshyn, and Minister of External Affairs Joe Clark opposed the bill, whereas…
text: The House of Commons of Canada is the lower house of the Parliament of Canada. Together with the King and the Senate of Canada, it forms the bicameral legislature of Canada.

title: Quebec City becomes the first city in North America to become a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
text: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization is a specialized agency of the United Nations (UN) with the aim of promoting world peace and security through international cooperation in education, arts, sciences and culture. It has 194 member states and 12 associate members, as well as partners in the non-governmental, intergovernmental and private sector.

title: Montreal is hit by a series of severe thunderstorms during the Montreal Flood of 1987.
text: The Montreal flood of 1987 happened on July 14 of that year when a series of strong thunderstorms crossed the island of Montreal, Quebec, Canada, between the noon hour and 2:30 p.m. Over 100 millimetres of rain fell during this very short period of time.

title: The Edmonton Tornado kills 27 people.
text: The Edmonton tornado, known as Black Friday to Edmontonians, was a powerful and devastating tornado that ripped through the eastern suburbs of Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, and parts of neighbouring Strathcona County on the afternoon of Friday, July 31, 1987. Six other tornadoes occurred in central Alberta the same day.

title: Ontario election: David Peterson's Liberals win a majority.
text: David Robert Peterson is a Canadian lawyer and former politician who served as the 20th premier of Ontario from 1985 to 1990. He was the first Liberal officeholder in 42 years, ending the Tory dynasty.

title: Pope John Paul II visits the Northwest Territories.
text: Pope John Paul II was the head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City from 16 October 1978 until his death in 2005. He was the first non-Italian pope since Adrian VI in the 16th century, as well as the third longest-serving pope in history, after St.

title: Canadian and American negotiators reach agreement on the Canadian-American Free Trade Agreement.
text: The Canada–United States Free Trade Agreement, official name as the Free Trade Agreement between Canada and the United States of America (French: Accord de libre-échange entre le Canada et les États-Unis d'Amérique), was a bilateral trade agreement reached by negotiators for Canada and the United States on October 4, 1987, and signed by the leaders of both countries on January 2, 1988. The agreement phased out a w…

title: Frank McKenna becomes premier of New Brunswick, replacing Richard Hatfield.
text: Francis Joseph McKenna is a Canadian businessman and former politician and diplomat. He is currently Chair of Brookfield Corporation and Deputy Chairman of the Toronto-Dominion Bank.

title: Dennis Patterson becomes government leader of the Northwest Territories, replacing Nick Sibbeston.
text: Nick G. Sibbeston is a retired Canadian politician, serving from 1985 to 1987 as the fourth premier of the Northwest Territories. Sibbeston was a Senator representing the Northwest Territories from 1999 until 2017, when he resigned on his 74th birthday, a year prior to reaching the mandatory retirement age.

title: Anthony Griffin is shot and killed in Montreal. Months of protests and two court cases ensue.
text: On November 17, 1987, unarmed 19-year old Black Canadian Anthony Griffin was shot and killed by Constable Allan Gosset of the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal outside of a police station in the Notre-Dame-de-Grâce neighbourhood of Montreal, Quebec, Canada. The killing led to months of community protests.

title: Several new Canadian specialty channels are licensed: YTV, VisionTV, CBC Newsworld, The Weather Network/MeteoMedia, and one pay-television channel: The Family Channel.
text: VisionTV is a Canadian English language Category A specialty channel that broadcasts multi-faith, multicultural, and general entertainment programming aimed at the 45 and over demographic. VisionTV is currently owned by ZoomerMedia, a company operated by Moses Znaimer.

title: Chartwell Technology company is founded in British Columbia.
text: Chartwell Technology was a gaming software developer focused largely on the online casino market. The company was based in Calgary.

title: ElderTreks, Canadian adventure travel company is founded.
text: ElderTreks is a Canadian adventure travel company for people over the age of 50.

title: Dave Duncan: A Rose-Red City
text: David John Duncan was a Canadian fantasy and science fiction author.

title: Michael Ignatieff: The Russian Album
text: Michael Grant Ignatieff is a Canadian author, academic and former politician who served as leader of the Liberal Party and leader of the Opposition from 2008 until 2011. Known for his work as a historian, Ignatieff has held senior academic posts at the universities of Cambridge, Oxford, Harvard, and Toronto.

title: Irving Layton: Fortunate Exile
text: Irving Peter Layton, OC was a Romanian-born Canadian poet. He was known for his "tell it like it is" style which won him a wide following but also made him enemies.

title: Donald Jack: This One's on Me
text: Donald Lamont Jack was an English and Canadian novelist and playwright.

title: Antonine Maillet: Margot la folle
text: Antonine Maillet was a Canadian novelist, playwright and scholar. She was a member of the Privy Council for Canada and the first non-European recipient of the Prix Goncourt, among other accolades.

title: Farley Mowat: Virunga: The Passion of Dian Fossey
text: Farley McGill Mowat was a Canadian writer and environmentalist. His works were translated into 52 languages, and he sold more than 17 million books.

title: Paul Quarrington, King Leary
text: Paul Lewis Quarrington was a Canadian novelist, playwright, screenwriter, filmmaker, musician, and educator.

title: Mordecai Richler: Jacob Two-Two and the Dinosaur
text: Mordecai Richler was a Canadian writer from Montreal, Quebec. He is best known for his novels set in Montreal's Jewish community; including The Apprenticeship of Duddy Kravitz (1959) and Barney's Version (1997).

title: See 1987 Governor General's Awards for a complete list of winners and finalists for those awards.
text: Each winner of the 1987 Governor General's Awards for Literary Merit received $5000 and a medal from the Governor General of Canada. The winners and nominees were selected by a panel of judges administered by the Canada Council for the Arts.

title: Books in Canada First Novel Award: Karen Lawrence, The Life of Helen Alone
text: The Amazon Canada First Novel Award, formerly the Amazon.ca First Novel Award and the Books in Canada First Novel Award, is a Canadian literary award, co-presented by Amazon.ca and The Walrus to the best first novel in English published the previous year by a citizen or resident of Canada. It has been awarded since 1976.

title: Gerald Lampert Award: Rosemary Sullivan, The Space a Name Makes
text: Rosemary Sullivan is a Canadian poet, biographer, and anthologist. She is also a professor emerita at the University of Toronto Mississauga.

title: Marian Engel Award: Audrey Thomas
text: The Writers' Trust Engel/Findley Award is a Canadian literary award, presented by the Writers' Trust of Canada to an established Canadian author to honour their body of work. Presented for the first time in 2008 under the name Notable Author Award, the award was created by merging the formerly separate Marian Engel Award and Timothy Findley Award, which were presented to female and male nominees respectively.

title: Pat Lowther Award: Heather Spears, How to Read Faces
text: The Pat Lowther Memorial Award is an annual Canadian literary award presented by the League of Canadian Poets to the year's best book of poetry by a Canadian woman. The award was established in 1980 to honour poet Pat Lowther, who was murdered by her husband in 1975.

title: Stephen Leacock Award: W.P. Kinsella, The Fencepost Chronicles
text: The Stephen Leacock Memorial Medal for Humour, also known as the Stephen Leacock Medal for Humour or just the Leacock Medal, is an annual Canadian literary award presented for the best book of humour written in English by a Canadian writer, published or self-published in the previous year. The silver medal, designed by sculptor Emanuel Hahn, is a tribute to well-known Canadian humorist Stephen Leacock and is accom…
wiki: Stephen Leacock Memorial Medal for Humour

title: Trillium Book Award: Michael Ondaatje, In the Skin of a Lion
text: Philip Michael Ondaatje is a Sri Lankan-born Canadian poet, fiction writer and essayist. Ondaatje's literary career began with his poetry: in 1967 he published The Dainty Monsters, and in 1970 the critically acclaimed The Collected Works of Billy the Kid.

title: Vicky Metcalf Award: Robert Munsch
text: Robert Norman Munsch is an American-born Canadian children's author. Born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, he moved to Canada in 1975 to work at the University of Guelph.

title: Rock band Cowboy Junkies record their most famous album, The Trinity Session, at Toronto's Church of the Holy Trinity.
text: Cowboy Junkies are an alternative country and folk rock band formed in Toronto, Ontario, Canada in 1985 by Alan Anton, Michael Timmins (songwriter, guitarist), Peter Timmins (drummer) and Margo Timmins (vocalist). The three Timminses are siblings, and Anton worked with Michael Timmins during their first couple of bands.

title: CityLine
text: CityLine is a Canadian talk show and lifestyle television program originally hosted by Dini Petty, who was then succeeded by Marilyn Denis and later Tracy Moore that aired from February 1984 until May 3, 2024, produced for the Citytv network at its Toronto flagship station CITY-DT. It also aired on its then-sister stations owned by CHUM Limited such as CKVR Barrie. Each show had a theme that changed daily.

title: Hot Shots
text: Hot Shots is a Canadian television drama series, which aired on CBS in the United States in 1986, and CTV in Canada in 1987. The series, produced by CTV for the CBS Late Night block of crime drama series, starred Dorothy Parke and Booth Savage as Amanda Reed and Jake West, crime journalists for the tabloid magazine Crime World.

title: Super Dave
text: Super Dave is a variety show starring and hosted by the fictional character Super Dave Osborne (played by Bob Einstein). It ran from 1987 to 1991 in the United States on Showtime and in Canada on the Global Television Network (then operating only in Ontario) and in first-run syndication (in all other parts of Canada).

title: On the Road Again
text: On the Road Again is a Canadian television series which aired from 1987 until 2007. Wayne Rostad was the program's host for its entire run.

title: CODCO
text: CODCO is a Canadian comedy troupe from Newfoundland, best known for a sketch comedy series which aired on CBC Television from 1988 to 1993. Founded as a theatrical revue in 1973, CODCO drew on the province's cultural history of self-deprecating "Newfie" humour, frequently focusing on the cod fishing industry.

title: Bumper Stumpers
text: Bumper Stumpers is a Canadian game show. Two teams of two players competed to decipher letter puzzles presented as fictional vanity licence plates.

title: Under the Umbrella Tree
text: Under the Umbrella Tree is a Canadian children's television series created by Noreen Young that originally aired on CBC Television from 1987 to 1993. It was produced by CBC and Noreen Young Productions, and later broadcast on The Disney Channel in the United States beginning on May 7, 1990.

title: Street Legal
text: Street Legal is a Canadian legal drama television series, which aired on CBC Television from 1987 to 1994, followed twenty-five years later by a six-episode season with a substantially different cast. Street Legal was the longest-running one-hour scripted drama in the history of Canadian television, holding the record for twenty years before being surpassed by the 139th episode of Heartland on March 29, 2015.

title: The Comedy Mill
text: The Comedy Mill is a Canadian sketch comedy television series, which aired from 1987 to 1991 on Hamilton, Ontario's CHCH-TV, and through syndication on other Canadian television stations. The show starred the husband and wife comedy duo of Steve Smith and Morag Smith, with a supporting cast that included Peter Keleghan, Linda Kash and Mag Ruffman.

title: Supernova 1987a is observed, the first "naked-eye" supernova since 1604.
text: SN 1987A was a Type II supernova in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a dwarf satellite galaxy of the Milky Way. It occurred approximately 51.4 kiloparsecs from Earth and was the closest observed supernova since Kepler's Supernova in 1604.

title: Asteroid 7816 Hanoi is discovered by Masahiro Koishikawa.
text: 7816 Hanoi, provisional designation 1987 YA, is an eccentric stony asteroid and Mars-crosser from the inner regions of the asteroid belt, approximately 3 kilometers in diameter. It was discovered on 18 December 1987, by Japanese astronomer Masahiro Koishikawa at the Ayashi Station of the Sendai Astronomical Observatory, Japan, and later named after the Vietnamese capital of Hanoi.

title: 10500 Nishi-koen is discovered.
text: The following is a partial list of minor planets, running from minor-planet number 10001 through 11000, inclusive. The primary data for this and other partial lists is based on JPL's "Small-Body Orbital Elements" and data available from the Minor Planet Center.

title: Musée d'art moderne (Saint-Étienne) opens as a separate institution.
text: The Musée d'art moderne et contemporain, or MAMC, is an art museum in Saint-Étienne, Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, France. It was inaugurated as a separate museum in 1987.

title: Palestinian cartoonist Naji al-Ali is shot in London; he dies 28 August.
text: Naji Salim Hussain Al-Ali was a Palestinian political cartoonist, noted for the political criticism of the Arab and Israeli regimes in his works. Al-Ali is best known as the creator of the character Handala, a personification of the Palestinian people that has become a prominent symbol of Palestinian nationalism and resistance.
